title: Lab 3: ExifTool Forensic Extraction & Document Provenance Audit
scenario: A leaked corporate PDF and an associated smartphone JPEG have surfaced on a public whistleblowing repo. Your task is to use command-line ExifTool to extract hidden forensic artifacts, determine the author's internal workstation identity, and locate the physical coordinates where the photograph was captured.

fields.label: Camera Serial & Model Identification
fields.prompt: Run ExifTool on the evidence file 'evidence_photo.jpg'. Extract the exact Camera Model, Lens Serial Number, and Firmware Version embedded in the MakerNotes.

fields.label: GPS Decimal Coordinates
fields.prompt: Extract the GPS Latitude and Longitude from the evidence image. Convert the coordinates into standard decimal degrees format (e.g., 40.542100, -80.012500) ready for mapping.

fields.label: Internal Author & Hostname Provenance
fields.prompt: Run ExifTool against 'internal_memo.pdf'. Extract the embedded Author username, Creator Tool, and original internal file path (if present in XMP metadata).

fields.label: Timestamp Discrepancy Analysis
fields.prompt: Compare the CreateDate and ModifyDate timestamps in the PDF header with the date written in the visible memo text. Is there evidence of backdating or post-dated modification? Record the exact time delta.

fields.label: Evidence Hash & Integrity Verification
fields.prompt: Compute the SHA-256 hash of the evidence file before and after metadata inspection to prove evidentiary integrity has been preserved. Enter the 64-character hex hash.
